ruth.2.p1.b1.text: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.

ruth.2.p1.b2.text: Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor.

ruth.2.p1.b4.text: So Ruth departed … And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.

ruth.2.p2.b4.text: She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab. … So she came out and has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter.

ruth.2.p3.b1.text: Listen, my daughter. Do not go and glean in another field, … but stay here close to my servant girls.

ruth.2.p3.b2.text: Indeed, I have ordered the young men not to touch you.

ruth.2.p3.b3.text: And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.

ruth.2.p4.b1.text: Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner?

ruth.2.p4.b2.text: I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, …

ruth.2.p4.b3.text: May the LORD repay your work, and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have taken refuge.”

ruth.2.p4.b4.text: My lord, … you have comforted and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not like one of your servant girls.

ruth.2.p5.b1.text: Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce.

ruth.2.p5.b2.text: she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

ruth.2.p5.b3.text: Even if she gathers among the sheaves, do not insult her. Rather, pull out for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather. Do not rebuke her.

ruth.2.p6.b1.text: So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. And when she beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley.

ruth.2.p6.b2.text: She picked up the grain and went into the town, where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi.

ruth.2.p7.b1.text: Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you.

ruth.2.p7.b2.text: The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz

ruth.2.p7.b3.text: May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead.

ruth.2.p7.b4.text: The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.

ruth.2.p8.b1.text: My daughter, it is good for you to work with his young women, so that nothing will happen to you in another field.

ruth.2.p8.b2.text: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain

ruth.2.p8.b3.text: until the barley and wheat harvests were finished.

ruth.2.p8.b4.text: And she lived with her mother-in-law.
